jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Whole-Ship Energy Modelling and Maritime Decarbonization
jobs.description:
SDU Mechanical Engineering (SDU ME), part of the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for an 18-month postdoctoral position in thermodynamics-based whole-ship energy modelling. The position is expected to start in March 2027, with the specific start date to be agreed upon with the successful candidate.

 

What we offer

You will join a research project titled Thermodynamics-Based Whole-Ship Energy Mapping for Retrofit-Oriented Maritime Decarbonization (STERN) funded by Den Danske Maritime Fond. STERN addresses a practical maritime engineering challenge: improvements to individual components do not necessarily result in optimal energy performance for the vessel as a whole. The project will develop physically consistent steady-state and dynamic energy models to quantify interactions among propulsion, auxiliary equipment, cooling and heating systems, waste heat and energy storage under representative operating conditions.

The postdoc will work within an interdisciplinary SDU team led by Assistant Professor Baris Burak Kanbur, together with Professor Marie Lützen and Associate Professor Paride Gullo, and collaborate with maritime partners including the shipping company Hafnia, DESMI and Fredericia Maskinmesterskole (FMS). ShippingLab will support maritime knowledge exchange and outreach. The position offers opportunities for independent scientific development, high-quality publications and close interaction with industry.

 

Main research activities

• 
Develop modular steady-state thermodynamic and energy-balance models for whole-ship energy mapping, covering fuel input, propulsion, auxiliary power, thermal loads, heat rejection and recoverable energy streams.

• 
Extend these models to dynamic energy simulations representing time-varying engine loads, operational profiles, mode transitions and relevant subsystem interactions.

• 
Model and analyze selected marine subsystems and energy-integration pathways, including propulsion-related energy demand, waste heat recovery, HVAC, cooling/heating optimization, thermal storage and battery storage.

• 
Use representative vessel and component data, engineering correlations and partner feedback to check model assumptions, quantify uncertainty and compare baseline and retrofit-oriented scenarios in terms of energy use and emissions.

• 
Contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations, project meetings, reporting and dissemination of non-confidential results.

 

Required qualifications

• 
A PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Energy Engineering, Thermal Engineering or a closely related engineering discipline (completed by the date of employment).

• 
A strong foundation in thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics (thermo-fluids) and energy-system analysis.

• 
Demonstrated experience in numerical thermodynamic or energy-system modelling, including steady-state analysis and time-dependent/dynamic simulation.

• 
Programming or modelling skills in MATLAB, Python or comparable scientific computing environments, with the ability to develop and document reproducible models.

• 
Knowledge of waste heat recovery, refrigeration/HVAC, cooling and heating networks, energy storage or component performance maps.

• 
Ability to conduct independent research, work with an interdisciplinary team and communicate research results effectively in English.

 

Qualifications considered an advantage

• 
Experience with marine engines, propulsion systems, ship energy systems or vessel operating profiles.

• 
Experience with dynamic simulation and control environment like MATLAB Simulink, Modelica/Dymola or equivalent modelling frameworks can also be considered.

• 
Knowledge of advanced control engineering, optimization or model-based control approaches, and experience collaborating with industrial partners.

 

Workplace description 

The position is full-time at SDU ME and located at the SDU main campus in Odense. SDU Odense is the university’s largest campus and provides a strong framework for interdisciplinary research, teaching, and innovation. You will be part of a modern workplace with high professionalism, strong academic communities, and a commitment to diversity and equal opportunities. SDU also offers dedicated support for International Staff. Learn more about careers and work life at SDU here: Careers at SDU.

SDU ME is part of the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering (IME) at the Faculty of Engineering. The research activities at SDU ME span widely from fluid mechanics, multi-physics simulation and optimization to condition monitoring and structural dynamics, composite materials, mechanical design, and naval architecture and marine engineering. 

The research environment combines thermo-fluid science, energy engineering and computational modelling, with collaboration across SDU and external maritime partners. The successful candidate will contribute to an industry-informed research project while working closely with academic colleagues and maritime experts. The research group is also part of the broader maritime research community at SDU, providing opportunities for transdisciplinary collaboration across faculties through the SDU Maritime Centre.

Get a glimpse of (work)life through the eyes of some of our many excellent researchers at SDU in Odense. 

 

Further information 

For academic enquiries about the position and the STERN project, please contact Assistant Professor Baris Burak Kanbur (babk@sdu.dk ) SDU Mechanical Engineering.

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

• 
One page motivation letter.

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

• 
Complete list of publications.

• 
Three publications most relevant to the position.

• 
Name of three references.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

 

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is January 1, 2027, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an expert or assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as a postdoc is temporary for an initial 18-month period. The preferred start date is in early 2027 (exact date to be confirmed). Extension may be possible depending on available funding.

Employment as a postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

jobs.occupation: Assistant, Tenure-track Assistant, and Associate Professorships in Interactive Technology and AI Engineering
jobs.description:
SDU Centre for Software Technology in Vejle, part of the Software Engineering units at SDU situated at the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for one or more positions within interaction technology and AI engineering. The positions are open from beginning of 2027, and the specific start date will be agreed with the successful candidates.

What we offer

With a position at SDU, you will:

• 
be part of one of our dynamic research centres with both a national and international profile, while working in areas of tremendous potential and societal relevance;

• 
join collaborations across the university, as well as with national, international, and industrial research partners;

• 
help establish joint innovation projects in close collaboration with industry and the local society;

• 
help build up the research and educational environment;

• 
contribute to the teaching programmes in Interactive Technology and Software Engineering at the highest level for undergraduate and graduate students at SDU;

• 
join a harmonious workplace environment that is conducive to productivity, promotes creativity, and rewards and recognizes individuals and group achievement;

• 
have the opportunity to live and work in one of the happiest countries in the world that also offers excellent and free health and education systems.

What we expect

The focus of the SDU Centre for Software Technology is research and education in software engineering, interactive technology and artificial intelligence. We see these areas complementing each other to make way for the engineering of the next generation of reliable, intelligent and interactive software solutions. We are particularly interested in software operated in real life, systems that adapt at runtime, span embedded devices, edge infrastructure and the cloud, that people work with and trust, and that increasingly answer to regulation. This includes understanding how AI technologies and data-informed software development with a human-centred perspective can change the engineering of products and software infrastructures.

The positions are open in any of the interaction technology and AI engineering research areas of interest to the centres, which include:

• 
Human-Computer Interaction and Design

• 
Interactive Systems Engineering

• 
AI-based User Interface Technology (e.g. generative user interfaces)

• 
Human-AI collaboration (e.g. robotics)

• 
Human-Centred Technology Ethics and Human-Centred AI Ethics

• 
Human-Centred and Socio-Technical Software Engineering

• 
Domain-oriented Interaction Technology (e.g., medical, energy or manufacturing)

• 
User Interaction Technologies (e.g., augmented reality and wearable technology)

• 
AI Engineering (e.g. multi-modal machine learning)

• 
Domain-oriented AI Engineering (e.g., medical, energy or manufacturing).

Who we are looking for

We are looking for candidates who have demonstrated research excellence appropriate to their career stage, who show a clear path towards an independent and internationally recognised research programme, and who are able and willing to contribute to competitive national and international funding applications. We also expect an interest in working across disciplines, in supervising students and junior researchers, and in teaching and advising in software engineering at all levels.

We particularly welcome applications from candidates who publish in leading venues in the field, such as CHI (Human Factors in Computing Systems), DIS (Designing Interactive Systems), CSCW (Computer-Supported Cooperative Work), NordiCHI, UIST (User Interface Software & Technology), IUI, HRI (Human-Robot Interaction), TEI (Tangible Embedded Embodied Interaction), IDC (Interaction Design & Children), UbiComp (Ubiquitous Computing), PerCom, EICS, AAAI, WWW, ACM CIKM; and in journals such as IMWUT and IEEE TASE. If your work is more domain oriented and you therefore publish in leading venues within a specific domain, you are also very welcome to apply.

We expect applicants to hold a PhD in human-computer interaction, artificial intelligence, software engineering, computer science or a closely related discipline, completed before the application deadline. 

For the tenure-track assistant professor positions we expect at least one year of research experience beyond the PhD, gained in academia, at a research institute or in industry. Applicants must demonstrate a higher level of achievement in research and related professional activities than generally expected of assistant professor applicants, as well as the potential to attain international research excellence within their field and meet the criteria for employment as an associate professor during the tenure track assistant professorship.

For the associate professor positions we expect a research and teaching record corresponding to several years of independent work after the PhD, including documented teaching and supervision experience.

Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of Danish is not a requirement, and successful applicants will be offered Danish language courses.

Workplace description

The University of Southern Denmark

The University of Southern Denmark is one of the youngest universities in Denmark, founded in 1966. The university is founded around the goal of providing the right knowledge at the right time to support society. The university targets major, complex societal problems of a cross-disciplinary nature such as climate, welfare, health and technology, tackling these in collaboration across faculties.

The Faculty of Engineering

The Faculty of Engineering is driven by the urge to create value for and with society, by curiosity and by the will to create that which only a few could imagine would be possible. Through research, education and collaboration, it is the ambition of the faculty to nurture talent, address challenges, create possibilities, and promote sustainable development. The faculty is strongly engaged with national and international industries and organizations over a broad range of technical domains.

The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute

The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute is an internationally recognized institute, which has maintained a leading position in robotics for more than three decades. The department is the 2nd largest department at SDU, with more than 230 staff members and 1500 students. The institute has over the last decades expanded its activities in interactive technologies, artificial intelligence, and software engineering including building several strong research centres at the SDU campuses in Odense and Sønderborg and with the new centre also in Vejle. Thereby, the institute today covers a wide range of areas in robotics, software, AI, and applied informatics.

Hear about the vision behind SDU Vejle - and why you as a researcher should consider joining the journey.

Curious?

If you are interested in learning more about the position, please contact:

• 
Torben Worm (Head of Centres): tow@mmmi.sdu.dk

• 
Mikkel Baun Kjærgaard (Vice-Head of Centres): mbkj@mmmi.sdu.dk

• 
Noura Lena Howell: nouh@mmmi.sdu.dk

• 
Aparna Varde: apva@mmmi.sdu.dk

Application procedure

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and an application must include: 

• 
Cover letter.

• 
Curriculum Vitae.

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (copy of original and official English translation).

• 
Complete list of publications.

• 
Up to five most relevant publications to the position.

• 
A research statement.

• 
For assistant professor applicants: Summary and documentation of experience in teaching

• 
For associate professor applicants: Teaching Portfolio documenting teaching, learning, and supervision qualifications and approach. Any format is acceptable; see the Faculty's teaching portfolio page for inspiration.

• 
Up to three reference letters may be included (optional).

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included (optional).

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration no.) must be crossed out. All PDF files must be unlocked and allow binding and may not be password protected.

The application deadline is December 15, 2026, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET).

 

Tenure Track at the Faculty of Engineering, SDU
The Faculty of Engineering at SDU offers an attractive tenure track programme aimed at the most talented scholars who have established a high level in their current research and other professional work, and those who possess exceptional potential to achieve the highest international level within their research area.

Candidates enter at the assistant professor level and, upon successful completion, will be promoted to a permanent position as associate professor, subject to a positive assessment by an expert committee.  

This evaluation is based on an overall assessment of the candidate's academic achievements and potential. Indicators of relevant scholarly merits include documented ability to develop an independent and internationally recognized research profile, deliver high-quality teaching and supervision, contribute actively to the academic community, and demonstrate the potential to secure competitive external research funding and build an ambitious research programme. The evaluation may also consider the candidate's contributions to the strategic and organizational development of the department, including a willingness to engage in academic leadership and administrative responsibilities.

As part of the tenure-track programme, the Assistant Professor is expected to complete SDU's Lecturer Training Programme before the evaluation, unless an equivalent university-level programme has already been completed at another institution.

The programme includes annual performance reviews, a midterm evaluation by an expert panel, and a final academic assessment. If the final assessment is positive, the candidate will progress to a permanent position as associate professor. If the final evaluation is negative, the assistant professor may request one additional assessment within the last six months of employment. The tenure track period may be extended in connection with maternity, paternity, or adoption leave.

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU. Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.

Employment terms

Appointment as an assistant professor is temporary and for an initial 3-year period. 

Appointment as a tenure track assistant professor is temporary and for an initial 4-year period, with guaranteed assessment for a permanent position as associate professor during the final year of employment.

Appointment as an associate professor is permanent.

Employment requires academic qualifications at a minimum of PhD level at the time of employment, as well as scientific and teaching qualifications commensurate with the position level. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state included the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for assistant professor, tenure track assistant professor, or associate professor as described therein. 

During employment at assistant professor level (incl. tenure track), the candidate will complete the Lecturer Training Programme.

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation.

To support our advancements in deep learning and AI methods for medical image and clinical data analysis SDU Robotics invites applications for one or more associate professor position(s). The starting date is in March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter and will be agreed with the successful candidates. The workplace is at SDU's main campus in Odense, Denmark, and the work is expected to be primarily onsite.

 

What we offer

• 
An exciting opportunity to work at the cutting edge of robotics for real-world applications.

•

• 
Opportunities for professional growth and leadership.

The successful candidates will contribute to the unit’s current and future research projects and teaching activities. Key responsibilities include, for example to:

• 
Be able to collaborate with our experts and colleagues from SDU Robotics in the further development of our core technologies. 

•

•

The position as an associate professor involves primary responsibilities related to research (including the obligation to publish and disseminate scientific knowledge) and research-based teaching (including examination duties) – research and teaching obligations equally. Additionally, the role may encompass knowledge exchange with society, including participation in public debates. Furthermore, it may entail responsibilities such as research management, curriculum development, guidance, supervision, and scholarly assessment. The university determines the specific allocation of tasks, and the emphasis on these tasks may vary over time.

 

Profile and requirements
The candidates will participate in SDU Robotics' comprehensive research, and the position requires research experience within artificial intelligence and deep learning for medical applications. This includes documented knowledge within some of the following technologies/areas:

• 
Deep learning-based classification, segmentation and detection in 2D and 3D medical images.

•

•

We value teamwork, professional diligence, enthusiasm for robotics and the drive to adopt new skills and extended responsibilities. We offer an open, international team with flexible work organization and support for individual development.

SDU Robotics is part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), and located at the main Campus in Odense, at the core of the Odense Robotics Cluster involving 120+ startups and established companies in robotics. 

The aim of the group is to solve challenging research problems derived from real-life challenges by implementing novel robot solutions. We participate in implementing the results achieved in real solutions with end users like national hospitals, LEGO, Novo Nordisk and Universal Robots.

jobs.occupation: Kok til thailandsk køkken  /  Chef to Thai cuisine
jobs.description:
Kok til thailandsk køkken

Brænder du for det autentiske thailandske køkken, og trives du i et travlt og velorganiseret køkken med høje kvalitetskrav? Så er det måske dig, vi leder efter!

Hos Thai Wok i Valby har vi i over 20 år lavet frisklavet, velsmagende thaimad til vores mange faste kunder. Vi søger nu en dygtig og selvstændig kok til at indgå i vores faste køkkenteam.

Dine primære arbejdsopgaver:

• 
Tilberedning af autentiske thailandske retter fra bunden (herunder wokretter, karryretter, supper og forretter) efter vores opskrifter og standarder.

• 
Klargøring af de friske råvarer, forberedelse af saucer og forretter, samt tilsmagning.

• 
Varemodtagelse, kvalitetskontrol af råvarer samt medansvar for lagerstyring og bestilling.

• 
Opretholdelse af høj hygiejnestandard og egenkontrol i henhold til Fødevarestyrelsens regler.

• 
Samarbejde med det øvrige køkkenpersonale om en effektiv og god arbejdsdag.

Vi forestiller os, at du:

• 
Har solid praktisk erfaring som kok – gerne med speciale i eller indgående kendskab til det thailandske/asiatiske køkken.

• 
Kan bevare overblikket og det gode humør, når der er travlt i aften- og weekendtimerne.

• 
Arbejder struktureret, hygiejnisk og sætter en ære i, at hver eneste ret forlader køkkenet i høj kvalitet.

• 
Er mødestabil, ansvarsbevidst og en god holdspiller.

• 
Taler og forstår enten dansk, engelsk eller thai.

Vi tilbyder:

• 
En fast fuldtidsstilling (40 timer om ugen) i en veletableret og sund virksomhed.

• 
En uformel og venlig arbejdsplads med erfarne kollegaer, hvor vi hjælper hinanden.

• 
Løn efter kvalifikationer og gældende vilkår.

• 
Arbejdstider primært i eftermiddags- og aftentimerne samt weekender efter fast vagtplan.

--

Chef to Thai cuisine

Are you passionate about authentic Thai cuisine, and do you thrive in a busy and well-organized kitchen with high quality standards? Then maybe it's you we're looking for!

At Thai Wok in Valby, we have been preparing fresh, delicious Thai food for our many regular customers for over 20 years. We are now looking for a skilled and independent chef to join our permanent kitchen team.

Your primary tasks:

Cooking authentic Thai dishes from scratch (including stir-fries, curries, soups and starters) according to our recipes and standards.

Preparation of the fresh ingredients, preparation of sauces and starters, as well as flavouring.

Goods receipt, quality control of raw materials and co-responsibility for stock management and ordering.

Maintenance of high hygiene standards and self-control in accordance with the regulations of the Danish Veterinary and Food Administration.

Cooperation with the other kitchen staff for an efficient and good working day.

We imagine that you:

Has solid practical experience as a chef - preferably with a specialization in or in-depth knowledge of Thai/Asian cuisine.

Can maintain an overview and a good mood when it is busy in the evening and weekend hours.

Works in a structured, hygienic manner and takes pride in the fact that each and every dish leaves the kitchen in high quality.

Is stable in meetings, aware of responsibility and a good team player.

Speaks and understands either Danish, English or Thai.

We offer:

A permanent full-time position (40 hours per week) in a well-established and healthy company.

An informal and friendly workplace with experienced colleagues, where we help each other.

Salary according to qualifications and applicable conditions.

Working hours primarily in the afternoon and evening hours and weekends according to a fixed shift schedule.

jobs.description:
The Nordic Humanities Center for Challenge-Based Inquiry invites applications for a 2-year postdoc to be filled by February 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

In recent years, a set of overlapping but different concepts have been used to describe a more world-oriented direction of the research conducted at universities: applied science, mission-driven research, challenge-based inquiry etc. These concepts and methods take on specific forms when they are adopted in the humanities. From a sociology of science or history of science perspective, the postdoc is expected 1) to map recent years' transformation within the academy towards challenge-based approaches and specific initiatives in Denmark and the Nordic countries – with a focus on the humanities, 2) to map how Danish and Nordic scholars in the humanities themselves engage in and conceptualize research on societal challenges, how they cooperate with external partners, and what humanists themselves consider to be the possibilities and challenges of this type of research, 3) to conduct an individual research project within this area, and 4) to contribute to the activities and events in the center.

The Nordic Humanities Center for Challenge-Based Inquiry is an innovative and ambitious center of advanced study that fosters new ways of doing humanities research. The center has been established in a collaboration between the faculties of the Humanities at the University of Copenhagen and the University of Southern Denmark with the generous support of the A.P. Møller Foundation. Over the course of the next six years, the center will each year gather a group of scholars at the two universities to marshal insights from the humanities and develop new perspectives, nuances, frames, and narratives for one of the many local and global societal challenges such as, for example, inequality, war, health, artificial intelligence, or the climate crisis.

Safety is at the core of everything we do, and we are committed to protecting our people, partners, and the planet as we work towards a sustainable energy future.

So yes, working for us will change the energy sector – and may well change you too.

We know that our people are our greatest strength. We strive to build an inclusive workplace where everyone can be themselves, contribute their perspectives, and feel part of the team. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and believe that diverse teams help us find better solutions and move the energy transition forward.

Care to join the movement?

Change. With us.

Dig deep. Find the needle. Grow the margin.

Do you love diving into data until you find that opportunity that makes the impossible business case possible? Do you get a kick out of turning a small, complex and creative insight into real profitability? And do you want to be the analytical engine and enabler behind a growing portfolio? Then you might be our new Portfolio Specialist within parallel import.

Make a real difference to a growing portfolio

Our business is growing fast, with more products, more markets and more competition on both the sales and purchasing side. That is why we have established Portfolio Management: a cross-functional department that steers demand and supply for our active portfolio across our European markets.

As Portfolio Specialist, you will work side by side with our Portfolio Managers and continuously find new ways to improve the profitability and accessibility of our active portfolio through new and cheaper sourcing, higher product availability and adding existing products to new sales markets. You will collaborate closely with Business Development, Sales, Purchasing, and regulatory, and your work will combine structured portfolio reviews with ad hoc tasks when changes in demand or supply call for fast and focused action.

Your primary tasks

• Continuously review the active portfolio to identify opportunities for optimization and development within the regulatory framework of each market.

• Find new, cheaper and alternative sourcing options that strengthen both profitability and product availability.

• Identify new sales opportunities for existing products together with Sales.

• Prepare analyses and business cases that support the Portfolio Managers’ decisions.

• Handle ad hoc optimization of specific products when demand or supply shifts, and show where action creates the most value.

Who are you?

Curious, persistent and never satisfied with the first answer. You love working with data, lots of it, you find energy in adding profitability, and you keep digging until you find the needle in the haystack. You understand that every opportunity must hold up within the regulatory requirements of each market, and you naturally keep building your regulatory knowledge and market dynamic know-how, so your analysis stays focused on what is possible. You are structured enough to drive continuous portfolio reviews and flexible enough to switch gears when an urgent request lands on your desk. You build strong relationships across the business, share your insights generously and challenge assumptions across the value chain constructively.

You may have a degree in Business, Engineering, Economics, Supply Chain or similar, and preferably some experience with data analysis, business cases or pricing, ideally from pharma within parallel import or generics. Reporting to the Head of Portfolio Management, you will join a brand-new department with strong ambitions, high visibility and a direct impact on 2care4’s profitability. You will help shape that journey in a cooperative, informal culture where we share knowledge, use yesterday’s lessons to build a stronger tomorrow, and enjoy a good laugh along the way. You will get thorough onboarding, a manager who invests in your development and colleagues who are always ready to help, because when you grow, so does the portfolio.

Our head office in Esbjerg is your home base. You will work from Esbjerg at least two days a week, and during onboarding you will spend most of your time here, so you get the best possible start with the team and the business. Beyond that, you can use our growing office in Odense and work from home when it makes sense for you and the team. We believe the best results are created together, so most of your week will be spent at one of our offices. We value close communication and direct collaboration with our stakeholders and 5-15 days of traveling per year is expected.

Do you want to grow together?

Join Copenhagen Energy Trading as our new Machine Learning Engineer

Machine learning is becoming an increasingly important part of how we understand energy markets, improve forecasts, and make trading decisions. We are therefore looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to move our models from research to production, building robust, scalable pipelines that continuously improve our strategies.

At Copenhagen Energy Trading (CET), we combine deep market expertise with machine learning, quantitative research, data, and engineering to automate and optimise how we trade power. We’re a small, highly ambitious team based in central Copenhagen, specialising in power trading and asset management across Europe and North America. Technology is at the core of how we operate, supported by one of Europe’s most advanced automated and analytical trading environments for power markets.

The Opportunity

Energy markets produce vast amounts of data and are continuously shaped by weather, power production, transmission constraints, and market behaviour. Using that data meaningfully requires accurate models and reliable software and infrastructure that allow those models to run in production.

As our Machine Learning Engineer, you’ll work across machine learning and software development. Alongside quantitative researchers, software engineers and traders, you’ll build the production systems behind our ML pipelines, making our trading more performant, more reliable and more automated.

You’ll own the full lifecycle around the model: from data management to the pipelines and frameworks that deploy and monitor our models, keeping them reliable and adaptive as markets evolve. The opportunity for impact is large, and so is what it asks of you: dedication, real talent and the willingness to grind through hard problems. This is a hands-on engineering role at the centre of how CET uses machine learning to trade.

What You Will Do

• Strengthen our ML framework: Build and improve the framework our researchers use to build models and quantitative strategies.

• Build production-ready software: Design and develop reliable, scalable, and well-tested Python software that integrates machine learning into our internal trading platforms.

• Develop data infrastructure: Build and maintain data pipelines and storage solutions for ingesting, transforming, and serving diverse market and fundamental data.

• Ship and operate models: Take models from experiment to production, including deployment, serving, monitoring and experiment tracking

• Improve our ML and engineering practices: Help strengthen our approach to MLOps, testing, CI/CD, code reviews, and the wider model development lifecycle.

• Shape our technical solutions: Evaluate and introduce tools and technologies that improve how we develop, deploy, and operate machine learning solutions.

• Collaborate across disciplines: Work closely with quantitative researchers, traders, and software engineers to turn business and market needs into practical technical solutions.

• Build energy-market expertise: Develop a deep understanding of power markets and how machine learning, data, and software can improve trading decisions.

What We're Looking For

We value strong technical ability, sound judgement, curiosity, and motivation to learn. While we don't expect a perfect match, many of the following qualifications will help you succeed in the role:

• Strong software engineering skills: Experience building clean, scalable, tested, and production-ready software. Strong Python skills are essential, as Python is our primary development language.

• MLOps and development practices: Proficiency in Git, code reviews, CI/CD, experiment tracking, model deployment, and monitoring.

• Cloud computing: Experience with Azure, AWS, or GCP, ideally including relevant data and machine learning services.

• Problem-solving and communication: The ability to structure complex problems, communicate clearly, and collaborate with colleagues across technical and commercial disciplines. Full professional proficiency in English is required.

• Ownership: The ability to work independently and deliver in a fast-paced environment.

• Interest in energy markets: Curiosity about power markets, trading, and energy systems. Previous experience in energy or trading is an advantage, but not a requirement.

• Education: A degree with a strong technical focus, e.g., Computer Science, Software Engineering, or other relevant fields. We welcome different educational backgrounds and levels of qualification.

What We Offer

• Growth environment: Become part of a young, ambitious, and expanding tech-driven trading company where talented people are given responsibility and room to grow.

• Exceptional team: Work closely with experienced quantitative researchers, software engineers and power traders.

• Competitive compensation: Receive a competitive salary package and attractive benefits that reflect your skills and contributions.

• Strong culture: Participate in both social and professional events, including team sports, company parties, team-building, and informal gatherings that strengthen our team spirit.

• Central Copenhagen location: Work from our office in Carlsberg Byen, located in beautifully renovated historic Carlsberg buildings.

How to Apply

If this opportunity feels like the right fit for you, we would love to hear from you.

Please apply via LinkedIn and submit your cover letter, CV, and university transcripts as a single PDF. Please note that applications that do not meet these requirements may not be considered.

Application deadline: November 27, 2026

Create the solutions that will enable a better tomorrow

You will help ensure that both internal project documentation and supplier documentation are collected, organised and securely archived. Following an introduction to the relevant processes, methods and systems, you will work with minimal supervision to ensure complete project documentation through to final handover and project closure.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Set up archiving structures in the customer's electronic document and records management system and clarify which documentation must be collected and retained.

• Collect and secure internal project documentation from customer-managed SharePoint sites, as well as photographic documentation and other project records.

• Collect and secure supplier documentation, including collaborating with the customer's IT team on developing APIs or automation tools where needed.

• Ensure that final as-built documentation is complete, that projects comply with the customer's archiving guidelines, and that sites and platforms are closed down at project completion.

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

• At least five years of experience in document control.

• Experience with electronic document management (EDM) systems, an aptitude for IT and a good working knowledge of Microsoft Office
